title: Hydromorphone for a vertebral fracture with docusate alone: no bowel regimen

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved 2026-11-16 (#202) the O3 review points of #201 as presented: the case and reference answer, the reviewed reason. The basis is SHM consensus statement 10 as quoted in #201, read by Claude Code in PubMed Central; the owner did not report reading the statement.

story: A 78-year-old woman with osteoporosis is admitted for pain control after an osteoporotic compression fracture of T12. She has hydromorphone 2 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed and scheduled acetaminophen. The admission order set added docusate 100 mg twice daily. She has had no bowel movement in two days, has no diarrhea, and her mobility is limited by pain.

encounter.reason: Back pain after lifting a laundry basket

problems.title: Age-related osteoporosis with current pathological fracture of vertebra

prescriptions.instructions: 2 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed for pain
100 mg by mouth twice daily (admission order set)

expected_findings.summary: No stimulant or osmotic laxative is ordered with hydromorphone; docusate alone, a stool softener, is not a bowel regimen.

reference_answer: Add a stimulant laxative, for example senna 8.6 mg, two tablets at bedtime, with polyethylene glycol 17 g daily if she has no bowel movement; the docusate can stop. Track bowel movements and adjust.
rationale: SHM's consensus statement 10 recommends a bowel regimen for hospitalized patients receiving opioids unless contraindicated (no diarrhea here), names stimulant and osmotic laxatives, and does not recommend stool softeners. The rule needs an active opioid order and no active stimulant or osmotic laxative order; docusate does not count.

citations.supports: Consensus statement 10: a bowel regimen for hospitalized patients receiving opioids; stimulant or osmotic laxatives; stool softeners not recommended. Read in the PubMed Central full text by Claude Code; owner approved 2026-11-16 (#202).
